court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Restrictive covenant against erecting a 'tenement house' not violated by construction of a superior apartment house; case turns on the distinction between tenement and apartment houses, not on letting of rooms for pay.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/tenement-vs-apartment-house construction dispute; no discussion of letting rooms or lodging arrangements.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Municipal ordinance restricting hours for peddling farm produce held void as class legislation and restraint of trade.
notes: Peddler-licensing ordinance case; unrelated to lodging/boarding or letting of dwellings.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Sustains constitutionality of the metropolitan elections district Superintendent of Elections statute against a home-rule challenge; the statute empowers deputies to inspect lodging houses/hotels and require lodger registers for election-fraud investigation.
notes: Election-law/home-rule constitutional case; 'lodging house' appears only as an object of election-fraud inspection powers, not adjudicating letting practices themselves.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Injunction pendente lite against a stockholder should restrain transfer of stock but not voting or other incidents of stock ownership.
notes: Corporate stock injunction case; 'incident of ownership' refers to stock rights, not real property letting.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Landlord's entry to repair a dangerous wall, pursuant to a lease clause permitting repairs, did not constitute eviction excusing the commercial tenant from paying rent.
notes: Commercial (manufacturing) lease eviction dispute; not about letting rooms or dwellings to lodgers/boarders.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Landlord who dispossessed a hotel tenant and retained/used the tenant's personal property (wines, supplies) via the hotel steward was liable for conversion; goods were not abandoned.
notes: Tenant here was the business lessee of an entire hotel (Cambridge Hotel), not a lodger/boarder; dispute is conversion of chattels on dispossession, not the character of a letting arrangement.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Stockholder enjoined from transferring/voting stock was not in contempt for joining another action to compel directors to restore corporate property, since that action was for the corporation's benefit.
notes: Corporate contempt/stock injunction sequel case; unrelated to property letting.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Vendee's acceptance of goods delivered late does not waive a counterclaim for delay damages; amended answer pleading such counterclaim should not have been struck as dilatory.
notes: Sale-of-goods/pleading practice case; unrelated to property letting or lodging.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Trustee who operated an apartment hotel with trust funds without clear authority to do so should not be permitted to amend its account to substitute net profits for itemized receipts/disbursements absent an allegation that the business was unauthorized.
notes: Trust-accounting dispute concerning a trustee's operation of an apartment hotel business; the property being an 'apartment hotel' is incidental background, not adjudicated letting/lodging doctrine.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: The court held that a residuary bequest to 'the person... that takes care of me in my last illness and that will remain with me and prepare me for a Christian death' was void for uncertainty as to the beneficiary. Even if the clause were valid, the plaintiff, a lodging and boarding-house keeper in whose house the testator lodged and died, failed to show she was the intended beneficiary, because she was presumed to have been paid for her services as a boarding-house keeper rather than acting as a gratuitous caretaker.

quotes.text: The plaintiff was at the time of the rendering of the above services a lodging and boarding-house keeper, and while there is no direct evidence upon this point there is a strong presumption that plaintiff was paid for her services, and, therefore, cannot be said to be the one the testator intended as his residuary legatee.

The plaintiff was at the time of the rendering of the above services a lodging and boarding-house keeper, and while there is no direct evidence upon this point there is a strong presumption that plaintiff was paid for her services, and, therefore, cannot be said to be the one the testator intended as his residuary legatee.

In any event a boarding house keeper in whose house the testator lodged during his last illness cannot identify herself as the beneficiary intended, for the presurhption is that.she was paid for any services rendered.

notes: Primarily a will-construction case; relevance is secondary — the court treats lodging/boarding-house keeping as an ordinary paid occupation, presuming compensation for the keeper's services to a lodger.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A restrictive covenant against 'any noxious, offensive or dangerous trade or business' constitutes an incumbrance defeating specific performance of a contract to convey title free of incumbrances.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/marketable-title case concerning offensive trades generally; no connection to letting rooms or lodging houses.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A hotel owner failed to establish a right of way by adverse user or necessity over a bridge on neighboring land used to access a dock, because the bridge was built and used under a revocable license and other access routes existed.
notes: Easement/way-of-necessity dispute involving a large summer hotel; mentions 'transient guests and regular boarders' only as background describing the hotel's business, not adjudicating lodging law.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A default judgment in summary dispossess proceedings is conclusive as to tenancy and non-payment of rent in a later action; a statutory receiver of a corporation who took possession under a lease is liable for rent as tenant.
notes: Commercial bank-premises lease/receiver liability case; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting of dwellings.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: The Appellate Division held that a hotelkeeper may lawfully sell liquor on Sunday only to bona fide hotel guests as statutorily defined: one who in good faith occupies a room, or one who during regular meal hours resorts to the hotel to obtain, and in good faith actually orders and obtains, a meal. Because the defendant's patrons were served liquor alongside uneaten sandwiches lacking the usual accessories of a meal, in a room people entered and left freely, the finding that she was serving genuine hotel guests could not be sustained, and the liquor tax certificate was ordered revoked.

quotes.text: and the term ‘ hotel ’ as used in this act shall mean a building regularly used and kept open as such for the feeding and lodging of guests, where all who conduct themselves properly and who are able and ready to pay for their entertainment, are received if there be accommodations for, them, and who, without any stipulated engagement as to the duration of their stay, or as to the rate of compensation, are, while there, supplied, at a reasonable charge, with their meals, lodgings, refreshment and such service and attention as are necessarily incident to the use of the place as a temporary home, and in which the only other dwellers shall be the family and servants .of the hotel keeper.

A guest of a hotel, within .the meaning of this exception to section thirty-one of this act, is : 1. A person who in good faith occupies a room in á hotel * *. * ; or, 2. A person who, during the hours when meals are regularly served therein, resorts "to the hotel for the purpose of obtaining and actually orders and obtains at such time, in good faith, a meal therein.”

It follows, therefore, that the judgment and order appealed from must be reversed, with ten dollars costs and disbursements, and the motion to revoke the liquor tax certificate granted, with ten dollars costs.

notes: Liquor Tax Law case turning on the statutory definition of 'hotel' and 'guest'; relevant for its articulation of transient lodging/innkeeping character and regulatory enforcement against the commercial operator, though the underlying regulated conduct is liquor sale rather than lodging itself.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Companion case modifying an injunction to strike the provision restraining a corporate defendant from voting stock, consistent with the related Alexander decision.
notes: Corporate stock injunction companion case; unrelated to property letting.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A restrictive covenant limiting use to private residences, imposed by a common grantor, was extinguished by merger of title when the tract passed through a single subsequent owner who conveyed the subdivided lots without reimposing reciprocal restrictions.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/merger-of-title case about converting a private residence into a store with offices; not about letting rooms to lodgers/boarders.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Landlord who withheld keys and refused possession unless the tenant paid for plumbing repairs breached the covenant for quiet enjoyment; jury verdict for damages reinstated.
notes: Commercial building lease/quiet-enjoyment dispute; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting of dwellings.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Loan commissioners lacked statutory power to lease State-owned farm land after 1897; summary dispossess proceeding could not be maintained where no landlord-tenant relation was validly created, and evidentiary error also required reversal.
notes: Farm-lease authority dispute involving State loan commissioners; unrelated to lodging/boarding of dwellings.
